targetTexts.1: This is the burden against Tyre: Wail, O ships of Tarshish, for Tyre is laid waste, without house or harbor. Word has reached them from the land of Cyprus.
targetTexts.2: Be silent, O dwellers of the coastland, you merchants of Sidon, whose traders have crossed the sea.
targetTexts.3: On the great waters came the grain of Shihor; the harvest of the Nile was the revenue of Tyre; she was the merchant of the nations.
targetTexts.4: Be ashamed, O Sidon, the stronghold of the sea, for the sea has spoken: “I have not been in labor or given birth. I have not raised young men or brought up young women.”
targetTexts.5: When the report reaches Egypt, they will writhe in agony over the news of Tyre.
targetTexts.6: Cross over to Tarshish; wail, O inhabitants of the coastland!
targetTexts.7: Is this your jubilant city, whose origin is from antiquity, whose feet have taken her to settle far away?
targetTexts.8: Who planned this against Tyre, the bestower of crowns, whose traders are princes, whose merchants are renowned on the earth?
targetTexts.9: The LORD of Hosts planned it, to defile all its glorious beauty, to disgrace all the renowned of the earth.
targetTexts.10: Cultivate your land like the Nile, O Daughter of Tarshish; there is no longer a harbor.
targetTexts.11: The LORD has stretched out His hand over the sea; He has made kingdoms tremble. He has given a command that the strongholds of Canaan be destroyed.
targetTexts.12: He said, “You shall rejoice no more, O oppressed Virgin Daughter of Sidon. Get up and cross over to Cyprus—even there you will find no rest.”
targetTexts.13: Look at the land of the Chaldeans—a people now of no account. The Assyrians destined it for the desert creatures; they set up their siege towers and stripped its palaces. They brought it to ruin.
targetTexts.14: Wail, O ships of Tarshish, for your harbor has been destroyed!
targetTexts.15: At that time Tyre will be forgotten for seventy years—the span of a king’s life. But at the end of seventy years, it will happen to Tyre as in the song of the harlot:
targetTexts.16: “Take up your harp, stroll through the city, O forgotten harlot. Make sweet melody, sing many a song, so you will be remembered.”
targetTexts.17: And at the end of seventy years, the LORD will restore Tyre. Then she will return to hire as a prostitute and sell herself to all the kingdoms on the face of the earth.
targetTexts.18: Yet her profits and wages will be set apart to the LORD; they will not be stored or saved, for her profit will go to those who live before the LORD, for abundant food and fine clothing.
